item.title: 26SSEIT22001-Subscription of 3 Consumer Data Statara Licenses
item.description:
Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration | Procurement | Award | $99K | Vendor: Compulink Technologies Inc In plain English (machine-written): The Human Resources Administration awarded Compulink Technologies Inc a $99,495 contract, without open competition as a minority- or women-owned small business, to subscribe to three licenses for the Statara consumer dataset, which the notice says helps the city reach underserved New Yorkers during emergencies.

The Statara consumer dataset provides information on over 5.5 million adult New Yorkers. This serves as a single data source that provides far broader coverage than PEU can get from various partner agency sources. Having this broad coverage is critical during emergencies and also helps PEU reach New Yorkers who have fewer existing touchpoints with the City. Without the consumer file in question, PEUs efforts to reach out to underserved New Yorkers, especially during and after emergencies, will be greatly impaired. This procurement is therefore necessary for continuation of critical agency functions, a Mayoral Priority, and directly related to public health and safety. An annual license for a consumer detail analytics file install, including updated and refreshed cell phone contact data available for NYC to house in your internal analytics database. This will include NYC residents that may be overlooked on traditional publicly available and privately sourced data sets. An annual license for consumer details to house inside of your separately licensed CRM database.

item.title: 6 Month NAE with Safe Horizon Inc. for CVAP
item.description:
Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration | Procurement | Intent to Award | Due: 2026-09-21 In plain English (machine-written): The Human Resources Administration intends to extend its contract with Safe Horizon Inc. for six months, from Jan. 1 through June 30, 2027, for $9,527,801.88 to continue the Crime Victims Advocate Program.

On behalf of the Mayors Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence (ENDGBV), the Department Social Services (DSS) intends to enter into a Negotiated Acquisition Extension (NAE) contract with Safe Horizon, Inc. to extend the contract for the Crime Victims Advocate Program (CVAP) by 6 months. CVAP places victim advocates for survivors of domestic violence and additional advocates for victims of every other category of crime in precincts and Housing Police Service Areas citywide. Advocates provide supportive counseling, connections to individual or group therapy, and help navigating the legal and financial challenges that can emerge after a crime has occurred. CVAP represents the Citys largest single investment in supportive services for victims of crime and regularly reaches more than 40,000 crime victims annually.

The proposed NAE term will be from 1/1/2027 through 6/30/2027 with a contract amount of $9,527,801.88.

Procurement and award are in accordance with PPB Rule Section 3-04(b)(2)(iii) for the reasons set forth herein.

item.title: Case Management Services - Staten Island
item.description:
Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration | Procurement | Award | $500K | Vendor: Caring Homes for the Homeless Inc In plain English (machine-written): The Human Resources Administration awarded Caring Homes for the Homeless Inc a $500,000 contract, chosen from competing proposals from a pre-qualified list, to provide emergency case management to Staten Island disaster survivors.

DSS/HRA goals  are to provide emergency and on-call case management services to victims affected by a large-scale disaster or other emergencies. Case managers would facilitate the delivery of appropriate resources and services. The selected proposers would work with disaster survivors to develop and carry out a client-specific recovery plan with the goal of stabilization and a return to normalcy. This partnership would facilitate client access to a range of resources. The services to be provided may include an assessment of the client verified disaster-caused unmet needs; development of a goal-oriented plan; organization and coordination of information on available resources; monitoring progress toward reaching the recovery plan goals; and, when necessary, client advocacy. Competition pool 5 Staten Island

item.title: Respect & Responsibility Services Program Comp Pool BK, SI
item.description:
Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration | Procurement | Award | $2.1M | Vendor: Justice Innovation Inc In plain English (machine-written): The Human Resources Administration awarded Justice Innovation Inc a $2,081,250 contract to run the Respect and Responsibility program, a community-based service for people who cause harm in their relationships, through a competitive proposal process limited to pre-qualified vendors.

Respect and Responsibility is a key component of a larger Interrupting Violence at Home initiative, which was launched in 2018 and focuses on addressing intergenerational cycles of abuse through non-mandated community-based programming for people who cause harm. It is one of the first programs of its kind in the country and reflects the culmination of years of work led by ENDGBV, with City agencies, survivors, experts, and advocates and its partner agencies to develop new pathways to hold harm doers accountable. Working with people who cause harm is a critical component in New York City efforts to interrupt intimate partner violence, support survivors, and foster equitable, peaceful, and consent-driven relationships and communities. Recognizing the need for diverse and effective programming for this population, in 2018, the City launched the Interrupting Violence at Home initiative. A central part of this Initiative is the non-mandated, community-based programming for people causing harm in their relationships the Respect and Responsibility program. Respect and Responsibility will be administered by the Mayor Office to End Domestic and Gender-Based Violence (ENDGBV) in partners…

item.title: Affordable Housing Program Services for DSS Referred Households
item.description:
Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration | Procurement | Award | $8.0M | Vendor: Acacia Network Housing Inc In plain English (machine-written): The Human Resources Administration awarded Acacia Network Housing Inc a $7,983,099 contract, chosen from competing proposals within a pre-qualified list, to run affordable housing with social services for households referred by the city's Department of Social Services at 1035 Anderson Ave. in the Bronx.

The New York City Human Resources Administration  is seeking qualified vendors to operate and maintain permanent affordable housing for single individuals, adult families, and families with children experiencing homelessness. Clients to be served are individuals and families who require social services support in order to succeed in permanent housing but are not in need of nor eligible for supportive housing. The housing can consist of an entire building or a substantial number of units within one building; HRA anticipates the contractor would propose a minimum of fifty (50) units or not less than 80% of the residential units in a building, whichever is greater.  Monthly tenant rent will be inclusive of utilities.

item.title: Respect and Responsibility Services Program -Queens Comp
item.description:
Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration | Procurement | Award | $1.5M | Vendor: Arab-American Family Support Center Inc. In plain English (machine-written): The Human Resources Administration awarded a $1,518,750 contract to Arab-American Family Support Center Inc. for the Respect and Responsibility Services Program in Queens, a community-based program for people who cause harm in their relationships, selected from competing proposals drawn from a pre-qualified list.

Respect and Responsibility is a key component of the larger Interrupting Violence at Home initiative, which was launched in 2018 and focuses on addressing intergenerational cycles of abuse through non-mandated community-based programming for people who cause harm. It is one of the first programs of its kind in the country and reflects the culmination of years of work led by ENDGBV, with City agencies, survivors, experts, and advocates and its partner agencies to develop new pathways to hold harm doers accountable. A central part of this Initiative is the non-mandated, community based programming for people causing harm in their relationships the Respect and Responsibility program. Respect and Responsibility will be administered by the Mayors Office to End Domestic and Gender Based Violence (ENDGBV) in partnership with the New York City Department of Social Services/Human Resources Administration (DSS/HRA).

item.title: FY26 Required Source Contract with Hunger Free America for SNAP Outreach
item.description:
Dept. of Social Svcs/Human Resources Administration | Procurement | Intent to Award | Due: 2026-08-18 In plain English (machine-written): The Human Resources Administration intends to award Hunger Free America Inc. a $721,333 contract for SNAP outreach to low-income households, a contract the state requires, for Oct. 1, 2025 to Sept. 30, 2026.

The Human Resources Administration (HRA) intends to enter into a Required Source contract with Hunger Free America Inc. for SNAP Outreach to increase SNAP participation. SNAP Outreach is a 50 percent reimbursement program in which the New York State Office of Temporary and Disability Assistance (OTDA) reimburse approved, reasonable, and necessary SNAP Outreach expenditures. The Federal funding is granted with the understanding that this funding supports the implementation of outreach activities to inform low-income households about the availability, eligibility requirements, application procedures and the benefits of SNAP. OTDA funds this Required Source contract and authorizes HRA to contract with Hunger Free America Inc. The term of this contract is 10/1/2025 to 9/30/2026. The contract amount is $721,333.
